correctness.rationale: For every connected finite simple G and each p_e in (0,1), all edge subsets including the empty subset have positive weight. The Hilbert–Schmidt weighted variance identity forces any peripheral eigenoperator to commute with each subset unitary and forces its eigenvalue to be 1; outside pi Z the singleton propagator commutant equals that of edge transpositions generating all vertex permutations, hence exactly span{P,Q}. Power boundedness excludes a unit-circle Jordan block, proving exponential convergence to the unique trace-preserving projection with conserved Tr(Pρ). For P3 at integer-pi steps the full-graph spectrum {0,1,3} and singleton spectrum {0,0,2} give precisely the identity or P/Q pinching channel, yielding localization limits 1/3,5/9,1 as stated. Reconstructable analytic proof, plus 129 separately implemented finite-dimensional diagnostic assertion groups; tests do not prove the all-graph statement.

value.rationale: The original graph-percolation model left fixed positive-duration quantum ensemble mixing at a numerical/heuristic level. This theorem solves the all-finite-connected-graph dynamical channel limit for arbitrary interior edge probabilities and arbitrary initial density, while exposing a sharp physical sample-time obstruction where a localized P3 particle remembers its starting vertex (return 5/9 or 1 instead of 1/3). The quantified stroboscopic discontinuity and order-of-limits warning are structurally motivated, not a routine single-small-graph calculation. No rate uniform in graph size, other resonant graphs or trajectory-wise convergence is claimed.
